result.body:
Engine-lane step 2 of #680. `packages/engine/testing-conventions.toml`
`one_function_per_file.max_lines`: **60 -> 50**.

## The split

The gate binds on the largest *second* module-scope function sharing a file,
and #688 named the remaining ceiling: `crates.ts`, where
`scanDirtyOutsideManifest` (59 lines) sat beside `publishImpl`. It moves to
`handlers/scan-dirty-outside-manifest.ts` with its own colocated test.
`crates.ts` keeps one publish-level case pinning that `publish` still consults
the scan and refuses on a stray edit.

## Mutants the split surfaced

Putting the scan in a new file placed every one of its lines in the mutation
gate's diff scope for the first time, and 26 mutants survived. Three of the
four clusters were masked by redundant code rather than by weak assertions, so
they are gone rather than asserted:

- The artifacts-root branch hand-rolled the relative-and-forward-slash
  conversion `repoRelativePaths` already exists to do for exactly these path
  sets — its own doc comment names the artifacts root as one of the three.
  Both skip sets now go through it, and its drop-if-outside-cwd rule subsumes
  the `artifactsRel !== ''` guard whose empty-string mutants were
  unobservable.
- The artifacts and sibling skip loops were the same three-arm prefix test
  written twice. They become `isWithinDir`, which drops a third arm the prefix
  arm already implied.
- `rest.includes(' -> ') ? rest.split(' -> ').pop()! : rest` — splitting a
  non-rename row returns it unchanged, so the guard was redundant and its
  literal an equivalent mutant. The ternary is gone.

The fourth cluster was genuinely unasserted and is now pinned: a
minimum-width porcelain row (`XY p`, which the `< 4` guard must admit), and
the two one-sided-quote paths that separate `startsWith && endsWith` from
either arm alone. Diff-scoped mutation now reports 70 tested, 0 surviving.

## Where the lane stands

Not closable yet. At 40 three files tie for the next ceiling — `cli.ts`
(`printUsage` + `run`), `npm-platform.ts` (`npmPublish`, 44) and
`preflight.ts` (`readDeclaredRepoUrl`, 43) — so 50 is this step's floor and
the upstream default of 1 is still several steps out.

## Changelog

No entry. Nothing here is consumer-observable: the split is internal to
`packages/engine/src`, and the config is a repo-internal CI threshold, not
reusable-workflow inputs, `putitoutthere.toml` schema, trailer grammar, or tag
/ release shape. Both commits carry `skip-changelog:`.

## Verification (Node 24.18.0, pnpm 11.11.0)

- `pnpm lint` — clean, both packages
- `pnpm typecheck` — clean, both packages
- `pnpm test:unit` — engine 1857 passed / 150 files, ci 612 passed / 92 files
- `pnpm test:integration` — engine 209 passed / 38 files, ci 44 passed / 10 files
- `testing-conventions@0.0.115` engine gates: `one-function-per-file` at 50,
  `colocated-test --base`, `coverage --base`, `unit lint`, `integration lint`,
  and `mutation --base` (70 mutants, 0 surviving) all pass

Refs #680

name: putitoutthere matrix

# Internal reusable workflow: plan + build jobs.
#
# Consumer-facing workflows (`release.yml`, `build.yml`) call this
# workflow as `uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere/.github/workflows/_matrix.yml@v0`
# so the plan + build steps live in exactly one place. release.yml then
# adds its own `publish` job that consumes the matrix + has_pypi outputs;
# build.yml stops here. Single source of truth — every action pin, every
# `if:` guard on `matrix.kind` / `matrix.build` / `matrix.target`, every
# shell snippet — only exists in this file.
#
# Permissions: contents: read only. No `id-token: write`. The build path
# must never grow publish-capable bytes — see issue #272 design notes.
# A grep assertion in `actionlint.yml` guards against drift.
#
# Concurrency: callers own the concurrency group. release.yml uses a
# repository-keyed group with cancel-in-progress: false; build.yml uses
# a ref-keyed group with cancel-in-progress: true. Declaring concurrency
# here would double-gate runs.
#
# The `uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere@v0` call below resolves to the
# same git ref the workflow itself was loaded from, matching the
# contract release.yml documents in its own header.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      node_version:
        description: >-
          Node version for plan / publish runners and for kind = "npm"
          build steps. Default `24`.
        type: string
        default: '24'
      python_version:
        description: >-
          Deprecated (#369): superseded by per-package
          `python_versions` in `putitoutthere.toml` and by
          `requires-python` inference. `kind = "pypi"` build steps now
          read the Python version from the planned matrix row, not
          this input. Retained so existing callers don't break; it has
          no effect on pypi builds.
        type: string
        default: '3.12'
      release_packages:
        description: >-
          Manual-release spec forwarded to `plan`. Comma-separated
          `name[@<bump|version>]` entries; when set, change detection
          is bypassed and exactly the named packages are planned.
          Empty (the default) => normal change-detected planning.
        type: string
        default: ''
    outputs:
      matrix:
        description: >-
          The plan matrix as a JSON string. Empty matrices serialize to
          `'[]'`. Consumers (`release.yml`'s publish job) parse this
          via `fromJSON()` and gate downstream jobs on non-empty.
        value: ${{ jobs.plan.outputs.matrix }}
      has_pypi:
        description: >-
          `'true'` when the planned matrix contains any pypi rows, else
          `'false'`. release.yml re-exposes this as its own workflow_call
          output so consumers can gate their caller-side `pypi-publish`
          job; build.yml does not (pass/fail gate, no caller jobs).
        value: ${{ jobs.plan.outputs.has_pypi }}
      unpublished_kinds:
        description: >-
          JSON array of the registry kinds this run still has something to
          publish — `["crates","npm"]` — computed by `plan` from the same
          `handler.isPublished` the publish path dispatches through, so a
          package whose planned version is already live is absent. A kind
          whose registry could not be reached stays listed: "we could not
          tell" must not drop a credential the publish may still need.
          `release.yml` gates its crates.io OIDC exchange on this rather
          than on the matrix carrying a crates row — a row is present
          whenever the repo has a crate, published or not, which made
          idempotent re-runs demand a working trusted publisher for work
          they would skip (#622). `'[]'` when nothing is left to publish;
          empty string when the plan itself is empty (the publish job is
          skipped then, so there is no gate to answer).
        value: ${{ jobs.plan.outputs.unpublished_kinds }}

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.matrix }}
      has_pypi: ${{ steps.has-pypi.outputs.has_pypi }}
      # #622: written by the same `plan` step that writes `matrix`. The
      # publish/skip determination is the engine's — see
      # `src/unpublished-kinds.ts`, not a `grep` over the matrix here.
      unpublished_kinds: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.unpublished_kinds }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node_version }}

      - id: plan
        uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere@v0
        with:
          command: plan
          release_packages: ${{ inputs.release_packages }}

      # Compute a boolean "has_pypi" the consumer can gate their
      # caller-side pypi-publish job on. PyPI uploads run in the
      # caller's workflow context (not this reusable workflow) per
      # the warehouse#11096 architectural constraint — see
      # notes/audits/2026-04-28-pypi-tp-reusable-workflow-constraint.md.
      - id: has-pypi
        env:
          MATRIX: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.matrix }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Bash-safe substring check; the matrix is a JSON array of
          # objects each carrying a `kind` field.
          if printf '%s' "${MATRIX:-}" | grep -q '"kind":"pypi"'; then
            echo "has_pypi=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "has_pypi=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  build:
    needs: plan
    if: fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix || '[]')[0] != null
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix) }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runs_on }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      # #391: prime ~/.cargo and target/ from the previous matching run's
      # cache so per-target matrix cells don't cold-compile their full
      # Cargo dep graph on every PR — the dominant cost on bundle_cli,
      # napi, and maturin matrices (observed at 4-6 min per cell with no
      # Rust changes on a downstream consumer; full release-precheck
      # workflow ~8 min).
      #
      # Gated to fire only on rows that actually invoke cargo:
      #   - pypi/maturin non-sdist: maturin shells out to cargo (and
      #     covers the pypi bundle_cli sub-build, same row).
      #   - npm/napi: the consumer's `napi build` script calls cargo.
      #   - npm/bundled-cli non-main: engine's `cargo build` for the
      #     staged CLI binary.
      # Pure-Python sdist, pure-Python hatch wheels, npm vanilla, and
      # the bundled-cli `main` row produce no cargo work and skip the
      # cache.
      #
      # `shared-key: matrix.target` partitions the cache slot per target
      # triple so a write to one target's slot doesn't blow away the
      # next cell's. `workspaces` enumerates every Cargo.toml-bearing
      # path the matrix may touch: `matrix.path` for the consumer's
      # package crate (maturin / napi / single-crate bundled-cli) plus
      # `matrix.bundle_cli.crate_path` for the bundle_cli crate when
      # it lives in a separate dir from `matrix.path` (the dirsql shape).
      # The second line resolves to empty when bundle_cli is unset and
      # Swatinem silently skips it.
      - if: (matrix.kind == 'pypi' && matrix.build == 'maturin' && matrix.target != 'sdist') || (matrix.kind == 'npm' && matrix.build == 'napi') || (matrix.kind == 'npm' && matrix.build == 'bundled-cli' && matrix.target != 'main')
        name: cargo cache (#391)
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          shared-key: ${{ matrix.target }}
          workspaces: |
            ${{ matrix.path }}
            ${{ matrix.bundle_cli.crate_path }}

      # ---- pypi ----
      # #369: each pypi row carries its own `python_version` (the
      # planner fans the matrix across the package's supported set,
      # inferred from `requires-python` or pinned via
      # `python_versions`). setup-python provisions exactly that
      # interpreter; the maturin build step below selects it explicitly.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'pypi'
        uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python_version }}

      # #276: bump the version source on disk to matrix.version BEFORE
      # maturin reads it. Maturin reads [project].version from
      # pyproject.toml (or [package].version from a sibling Cargo.toml
      # when pyproject declares dynamic = ["version"]) at build time,
      # with no env override. Without this step, wheels ship at
      # whatever literal is in the consumer's manifest — diverging
      # from the planned version and tripping PyPI's "file already
      # exists" rejection at upload. crates / npm bump at publish;
      # setuptools-scm / hatch-vcs use SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION
      # below. Maturin is the only build path with no fallback, so
      # the bump has to live here.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'pypi' && matrix.build == 'maturin'
        uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere@v0
        with:
          command: write-version
          working_directory: ${{ matrix.path }}
          version: ${{ matrix.version }}

      # Two invocations: `maturin build --sdist` produces wheel AND sdist
      # (the flag is "also build sdist", not "only build sdist"), so the
      # sdist row would emit a wheel artifact that collides with the
      # per-target wheel rows at upload time. Use `command: sdist` for
      # the sdist row, which produces sdist-only.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'pypi' && matrix.build == 'maturin' && matrix.target == 'sdist'
        uses: PyO3/maturin-action@v1
        with:
          working-directory: ${{ matrix.path }}
          command: sdist
          args: --out dist

      # #282: bundle_cli — cross-compile a Rust CLI per target and stage
      # it into the package source tree so maturin's [tool.maturin].include
      # glob picks it up as wheel data. Without these steps, wheels for
      # consumers who declare `[package.bundle_cli]` ship without the
      # binary and `pip install <pkg> && <pkg> ...` fails at runtime with
      # FileNotFoundError. Sdist row is excluded — sdists are source-only.
      #
      # Targets resolve to native runners via `defaultRunsOn` in
      # `src/plan.ts`, so cargo cross-compile linkers are not needed:
      # x86_64-linux on ubuntu-latest, aarch64-linux on ubuntu-24.04-arm,
      # darwin on macos-latest, windows on windows-2022 (pinned; see #354).
      # Rust is pre-installed on all GHA runners; we only `rustup target add`
      # to make the triple known.
      # #603: compile the DECLARED triple — no gnu→musl mapping (the npm
      # bundled-cli lane below reaches the same property via zigbuild,
      # #605). A musl build is statically
      # linked (static-pie), and a static binary cannot dlopen: consumer
      # CLIs that load SQLite extensions fail at runtime with `Dynamic
      # loading not supported` (dirsql#755). The #381 portability concern
      # does not apply on pypi: the wheel's manylinux platform tag already
      # encodes the glibc floor of runner-built artifacts and pip refuses
      # to install the wheel anywhere older, so a dynamically-linked gnu
      # binary has exactly the wheel's own reach.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'pypi' && matrix.build == 'maturin' && matrix.bundle_cli && matrix.target != 'sdist'
        name: bundle_cli — add Rust target
        shell: bash
        env:
          TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          rustup target add "$TARGET"

      # #374: bump the separate bundle_cli crate's `[package].version`
      # before `cargo build` runs. The maturin `write-version` step
      # above bumps the Python package's version source; it does not
      # touch the CLI crate at `bundle_cli.crate_path`. cargo bakes
      # CARGO_PKG_VERSION from that crate's on-disk Cargo.toml at
      # compile time, so the staged binary must get the same direct
      # Cargo.toml rewrite as the npm bundled-cli path.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'pypi' && matrix.build == 'maturin' && matrix.bundle_cli && matrix.target != 'sdist'
        name: bundle_cli — write crate version for ${{ matrix.name }}
        uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere@v0
        with:
          command: write-crate-version
          working_directory: ${{ matrix.bundle_cli.crate_path }}
          version: ${{ matrix.version }}

      - if: matrix.kind == 'pypi' && matrix.build == 'maturin' && matrix.bundle_cli && matrix.target != 'sdist'
        name: bundle_cli — cargo build for ${{ matrix.target }} (${{ matrix.bundle_cli.bin }})
        shell: bash
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.bundle_cli.crate_path }}
        env:
          TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
          BIN: ${{ matrix.bundle_cli.bin }}
          # #300: support the lib-with-optional-CLI shape (ruff/uv/
          # pydantic-core/biome/swc/dirsql) where the binary lives behind
          # `[[bin]] required-features = ["cli"]`. Empty `features` and
          # `no_default_features = false` (the schema defaults) leave the
          # cargo invocation byte-identical to its pre-#300 form.
          FEATURES: ${{ join(matrix.bundle_cli.features, ',') }}
          NO_DEFAULT_FEATURES: ${{ matrix.bundle_cli.no_default_features }}
        # #337: pin `--target-dir target` so the produced binary lands at
        # `${CRATE_PATH}/target/<triple>/release/<bin>` regardless of
        # whether `crate_path` points at a workspace root or a member
        # crate. cargo's default target-dir is workspace-rooted; without
        # the explicit pin, the stage step below (which reads from
        # `${CRATE_PATH}/target/...`) can't find the binary whenever
        # the crate participates in a `[workspace]`.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # #603: see the `add Rust target` step above — the pypi lane
          # compiles the declared triple, never a musl mapping.
          args=(build --release --target "$TARGET" --bin "$BIN" --target-dir target)
          if [ -n "$FEATURES" ]; then args+=(--features "$FEATURES"); fi
          if [ "$NO_DEFAULT_FEATURES" = "true" ]; then args+=(--no-default-features); fi
          cargo "${args[@]}"

      - if: matrix.kind == 'pypi' && matrix.build == 'maturin' && matrix.bundle_cli && matrix.target != 'sdist'
        name: bundle_cli — stage binary into ${{ matrix.path }}/${{ matrix.bundle_cli.stage_to }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          CRATE_PATH: ${{ matrix.bundle_cli.crate_path }}
          PKG_PATH: ${{ matrix.path }}
          STAGE_TO: ${{ matrix.bundle_cli.stage_to }}
          BIN: ${{ matrix.bundle_cli.bin }}
          TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # #603: read from the declared triple's target dir cargo built into.
          if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = "Windows" ]; then ext=".exe"; else ext=""; fi
          src="${CRATE_PATH}/target/${TARGET}/release/${BIN}${ext}"
          dst_dir="${PKG_PATH}/${STAGE_TO}"
          if [ ! -f "$src" ]; then
            echo "::error::cargo build did not produce ${src}"
            ls -la "${CRATE_PATH}/target/${TARGET}/release/" || true
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p "$dst_dir"
          cp "$src" "$dst_dir/"
          echo "staged: $src -> $dst_dir/${BIN}${ext}"

      # #369: build the wheel for this row's specific CPython version.
      # When a manylinux container is in play it ships every CPython, so
      # the interpreter has to be selected explicitly — `-i <version>`
      # (a bare `3.12`) is resolved by maturin's interpreter scan (which
      # also finds the setup-python host interpreter on containerless
      # linux builds). macOS uses the host `python<version>` that
      # setup-python provisioned. Windows omits `-i` entirely: maturin's
      # non-container build there already uses the single host
      # interpreter setup-python pinned to this row's version.
      #
      # #610: `manylinux` forwards the row's platform-tag baseline (set
      # by `plan` from the package's `manylinux` config key, linux rows
      # only). Non-empty, maturin-action builds inside the matching
      # quay.io/pypa manylinux/musllinux container and passes
      # `--manylinux <value>`, so the wheel is tagged with the requested
      # baseline instead of the host's glibc (ubuntu-24.04 = 2.39 —
      # thekevinscott/dirsql#818). Empty (the default when the key is
      # absent), the input is a no-op and the build stays on the host,
      # byte-identical to the pre-#610 behavior.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'pypi' && matrix.build == 'maturin' && matrix.target != 'sdist'
        uses: PyO3/maturin-action@v1
        with:
          working-directory: ${{ matrix.path }}
          command: build
          manylinux: ${{ matrix.manylinux }}
          args: >-
            --release --out dist --target ${{ matrix.target }}
            ${{ runner.os == 'Linux' && format('--interpreter {0}', matrix.python_version)
                || (runner.os == 'macOS' && format('--interpreter python{0}', matrix.python_version) || '') }}

      # #282: wheel-content guard. Permanent defense-in-depth — the
      # produced wheel must contain the staged binary at <stage_to>/<bin>.
      # Catches the bug shape this issue tracks (no staging happened) and
      # any future regression where the cross-compile silently routes the
      # binary to the wrong path. Runs before upload-artifact, so a
      # broken wheel never leaves the build runner.
      #
      # Path-inside-wheel notes: maturin rewrites paths from the package
      # source root into the wheel's distribution layout. The exact path
      # depends on the consumer's pyproject layout (`python/<pkg>/...`
      # vs `src/<pkg>/...`), so we can't assert against a fully qualified
      # in-wheel path. We assert that *some* directory inside the wheel
      # ends in the consumer's `stage_to` and contains the named bin —
      # which is the strongest cross-layout assertion that still catches
      # "binary missing entirely."
      #
      # #338: when `[tool.maturin].python-source` is set (the standard
      # `maturin new --mixed` layout), maturin strips that prefix from
      # on-disk paths when rewriting them into the wheel's distribution
      # layout. A binary that lives on disk at
      # `<pkg.path>/<stage_to>/<bin>` = e.g. `packages/python/python/dirsql/_binary/dirsql`
      # ends up in the wheel at `dirsql/_binary/dirsql` — `python/`
      # stripped. The engine reads `python-source` from the consumer's
      # pyproject and subtracts it from `stage_to`; when unset/empty the
      # behaviour is identical.
      #
      # #595: this step used to carry the check inline — `unzip -l | awk |
      # grep`, plus a `python3 - <<PY … import tomllib … PY` heredoc for the
      # python-source parse. Both are gone; the engine has shipped the whole
      # check as `verify bundle-cli` since #451 (same wheel selection, same
      # python-source stripping, same match, same `::error::` / `ok
      # bundle_cli:` strings and exit code), and #595 gave `action.yml` the
      # `verify` surface that finally lets a reusable workflow call it. Two
      # defects died with the heredoc:
      #
      #   - It ran under whatever interpreter `setup-python` provisioned for
      #     this wheel row, and `tomllib` is stdlib only on CPython >= 3.11 —
      #     so every fanned wheel row with a <= 3.10 floor crashed the
      #     release build. The engine parses TOML on the action's own Node,
      #     which no `requires-python` floor can reach.
      #   - It was untested workflow YAML duplicating logic the engine
      #     already owned (`readPythonSource` + `computeStageSuffix`). The
      #     duplicate is deleted, not relocated — one tested implementation.
      #
      # The engine also reads the wheel with a pure-Node zip reader, so the
      # step no longer depends on `unzip` being on the runner.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'pypi' && matrix.build == 'maturin' && matrix.bundle_cli && matrix.target != 'sdist'
        name: bundle_cli — verify wheel contains ${{ matrix.bundle_cli.stage_to }}/${{ matrix.bundle_cli.bin }}
        uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere@v0
        with:
          command: verify-bundle-cli
          working_directory: ${{ matrix.path }}
          stage_to: ${{ matrix.bundle_cli.stage_to }}
          bin: ${{ matrix.bundle_cli.bin }}
          # The Rust target triple, not `RUNNER_OS`: the engine selects the
          # `.exe` suffix from a triple containing `windows`, which is the
          # same decision the bash made from `$RUNNER_OS = Windows` for
          # every row the maturin matrix builds.
          target: ${{ matrix.target }}

      - if: matrix.kind == 'pypi' && matrix.build != 'maturin' && matrix.target == 'sdist'
        # hatch-vcs / setuptools-scm derive the version from the latest git
        # tag at build time — which is still the *previous* release at this
        # point. Feed the planned version through setuptools-scm's global
        # pretend-version env so the sdist filename matches what we're about
        # to publish. Per-package variants are silently ignored by hatch-vcs;
        # only the global one works.
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.path }}
        env:
          SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION: ${{ matrix.version }}
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip build
          python -m build --sdist --outdir dist

      # #324: pure-Python hatch packages also produce an any-platform
      # wheel so PyPI ends up with both sdist and wheel. Without this,
      # downstream `pip install` / `uvx ...` had to provision hatchling
      # and run `python -m build` on a cold cache instead of doing a
      # sub-second download-and-extract. The wheel row is hatch-only
      # (see plan.ts); setuptools stays sdist-only, maturin keeps its
      # per-target wheel rows.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'pypi' && matrix.build == 'hatch' && matrix.target == 'any'
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.path }}
        env:
          SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION: ${{ matrix.version }}
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip build
          python -m build --wheel --outdir dist

      # ---- npm ----
      - if: matrix.kind == 'npm'
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node_version }}
          registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'

      # #299: bundled-cli launcher — author `bin/<bin>.js` +
      # `package.json#bin` for the main package before `npm run build`
      # runs. The launcher is templated on (pkg name, configured
      # targets) and identical across consumers; the engine writes it
      # in place, only if absent (so consumers can override either
      # piece). Same `working_directory` → `--path` plumbing as the
      # pypi write-version step above.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'npm' && matrix.build == 'bundled-cli' && matrix.target == 'main'
        name: write-launcher — generate bundled-cli launcher for ${{ matrix.name }}
        uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere@v0
        with:
          command: write-launcher
          working_directory: ${{ matrix.path }}

      # #298: bundle_cli — cross-compile a Rust CLI per target and stage
      # it under `${{ matrix.artifact_path }}` so the engine's npm-platform
      # handler packages it into the per-platform tarball. Same shape as
      # the maturin/pypi block above. Without these steps, npm bundled-cli
      # consumers are still required to author a `scripts/build.cjs` that
      # cargo-builds the binary themselves; absorbing the script removes
      # the largest remaining piece of consumer integration surface for
      # this recipe (#287 documented the seam between consumer scripts
      # and the engine env contract; #298 closes the seam entirely).
      #
      # Targets resolve to native runners via `defaultRunsOn` in
      # `src/plan.ts`, so cargo cross-compile linkers are not needed.
      # The `main` target row is the noarch top-level package — it has
      # no per-target binary to compile.
      # #605: like the pypi lane, the DECLARED triple is compiled — but via
      # cargo-zigbuild with a pinned glibc floor, since npm has no
      # install-time glibc gate (see the add-target step below).
      - if: matrix.kind == 'npm' && matrix.build == 'bundled-cli' && matrix.bundle_cli && matrix.target != 'main'
        name: bundle_cli — add Rust target
        shell: bash
        env:
          RUST_TARGET: ${{ matrix.rust_target }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # #387: matrix.rust_target is the engine-resolved Rust triple
          # (plan.ts maps the npm-flavor matrix.target via toRustTriple).
          # #605: register the DECLARED triple — no gnu→musl mapping. Linux
          # rows compile via cargo-zigbuild pinned to GLIBC_FLOOR, so the
          # binary stays dynamically linked (dlopen works, dirsql#762)
          # without inheriting the runner's glibc (#381).
          rustup target add "$RUST_TARGET"

      # #605: cargo-zigbuild links Linux binaries against a *chosen* glibc
      # (GLIBC_FLOOR) regardless of the runner's, replacing the #381
      # static-musl mapping — dynamic linking keeps dlopen working
      # (dirsql#762), the pinned floor keeps #381's portability. The
      # ziglang wheel supplies zig; cargo-zigbuild discovers it via
      # `python3 -m ziglang`. zig is a C cross-compiler too, so crates
      # with C source deps (libsqlite3-sys bundled, …) need no extra
      # toolchain.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'npm' && matrix.build == 'bundled-cli' && matrix.bundle_cli && matrix.target != 'main' && contains(matrix.target, 'linux')
        name: bundle_cli — install zigbuild toolchain
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          pip3 install cargo-zigbuild ziglang
          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      # #366: bump the crate's `[package].version` to matrix.version
      # before `cargo build` runs. `cargo build` bakes CARGO_PKG_VERSION
      # into the binary at compile time from the on-disk Cargo.toml,
      # with no env override — so without this step the cross-compiled
      # CLI reports the stale crate literal from `--version` instead of
      # the planned release version (e.g. `@scope/cli-<triple>@0.3.5`
      # shipping a binary that says `0.2.7`). Mirrors the maturin/pypi
      # `write-version` step above; `write-version` itself is
      # maturin-specific (it requires a `pyproject.toml`), so the npm
      # bundled-cli path uses the Cargo.toml-direct `write-crate-version`.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'npm' && matrix.build == 'bundled-cli' && matrix.bundle_cli && matrix.target != 'main'
        name: bundle_cli — write crate version for ${{ matrix.name }}
        uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere@v0
        with:
          command: write-crate-version
          working_directory: ${{ matrix.bundle_cli.crate_path }}
          version: ${{ matrix.version }}

      - if: matrix.kind == 'npm' && matrix.build == 'bundled-cli' && matrix.bundle_cli && matrix.target != 'main'
        name: bundle_cli — cargo build for ${{ matrix.target }} (${{ matrix.bundle_cli.bin }})
        shell: bash
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.bundle_cli.crate_path }}
        env:
          RUST_TARGET: ${{ matrix.rust_target }}
          BIN: ${{ matrix.bundle_cli.bin }}
          GLIBC_FLOOR: "2.17"
          # Mirror of the pypi shape (#300). Empty `features` and
          # `no_default_features = false` (schema defaults) leave the
          # cargo invocation byte-identical to its `--features`-less form.
          FEATURES: ${{ join(matrix.bundle_cli.features, ',') }}
          NO_DEFAULT_FEATURES: ${{ matrix.bundle_cli.no_default_features }}
        # Build the cargo invocation in a single non-empty array, mirroring
        # the pypi cargo-build step above. `cmd=()` followed by
        # `"${cmd[@]}"` on an empty array errors out under bash 3.2 + set
        # -u ("unbound variable") — and macOS runners ship bash 3.2 by
        # default. The array always starts with `(cargo build --release
        # ...)`, so the expansion is safe on every runner.
        #
        # #337: pin `--target-dir target` so the produced binary lands at
        # `${CRATE_PATH}/target/<triple>/release/<bin>` regardless of
        # whether `crate_path` points at a workspace root or a member
        # crate. Mirrors the pypi cargo-build step's fix; same workspace
        # target-dir bug shape, same resolution.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # #387: matrix.rust_target is the engine-resolved Rust triple
          # (plan.ts maps the npm-flavor matrix.target via toRustTriple).
          # #605: Linux rows build via cargo-zigbuild with the glibc floor
          # pinned in the target suffix, so the binary is dynamically
          # linked (dlopen works — dirsql#762) yet floors at GLIBC_FLOOR
          # instead of the runner's glibc (#381). zigbuild strips the
          # suffix from the output dir, so artifacts land at
          # target/<triple>/release/ either way.
          case "$RUST_TARGET" in
            *-linux-gnu*)
              cmd=(cargo zigbuild --release --target "${RUST_TARGET}.${GLIBC_FLOOR}" --bin "$BIN" --target-dir target)
              ;;
            *-linux-musl*)
              # A consumer that DECLARES a musl triple gets zigbuild too, with
              # no floor to pin — musl has no glibc, and `<triple>.2.17` is not
              # a target zig accepts. It still needs zig: zig ships musl, so it
              # is the C cross-compiler these rows used to get from the apt
              # `CC_<triple>=musl-gcc` step this one replaced. Falling through
              # to a plain `cargo build` leaves them with no C toolchain at
              # all, and every crate with C sources — the ones a musl consumer
              # is told to vendor — fails to link.
              cmd=(cargo zigbuild --release --target "$RUST_TARGET" --bin "$BIN" --target-dir target)
              ;;
            *)
              cmd=(cargo build --release --target "$RUST_TARGET" --bin "$BIN" --target-dir target)
              ;;
          esac
          if [ -n "$FEATURES" ]; then cmd+=(--features "$FEATURES"); fi
          if [ "$NO_DEFAULT_FEATURES" = "true" ]; then cmd+=(--no-default-features); fi
          "${cmd[@]}"

      # #429: bump the napi crate's version to matrix.version before
      # `napi build` (inside `npm run build`) bakes CARGO_PKG_VERSION into
      # the compiled `.node`. Mirror of the bundled-cli write-crate-version
      # step above (#366) and the maturin write-version step (#276): without
      # it the per-triple `.node` ships the stale on-disk crate literal, so
      # a library re-exposing the Rust core's version() through napi reports
      # a version diverging from the published npm package (whose synthesized
      # package.json version is already correct). #428: write-crate-version
      # resolves `version.workspace = true` to the workspace root, so a
      # polyglot-workspace napi crate is handled too.
      #
      # The bump runs only when the napi crate's Cargo.toml is COLOCATED at
      # the package path (the napi-rs single-crate default: Cargo.toml beside
      # package.json — the shape template-lib and the js-napi fixture use). A
      # multi-mode package (napi + bundled-cli) or one whose napi crate lives
      # elsewhere has no Cargo.toml at matrix.path, and there is no per-napi
      # `crate_path` config to point at it yet, so the bump is skipped with a
      # notice rather than guessed. The noarch `main` row compiles no
      # `.node`, so it is excluded.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'npm' && matrix.build == 'napi' && matrix.target != 'main'
        name: napi — detect colocated crate for ${{ matrix.name }}
        id: napi-crate
        shell: bash
        env:
          PKG_PATH: ${{ matrix.path }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -f "${PKG_PATH}/Cargo.toml" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::napi: no Cargo.toml at ${PKG_PATH} — skipping the pre-build crate-version write; the .node will embed its on-disk CARGO_PKG_VERSION. Colocate the napi crate's Cargo.toml with package.json to bake the release version in automatically (multi-mode / separate-crate napi is not yet auto-bumped)."
          fi
      - if: matrix.kind == 'npm' && matrix.build == 'napi' && matrix.target != 'main' && steps.napi-crate.outputs.present == 'true'
        name: napi — write crate version for ${{ matrix.name }}
        uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere@v0
        with:
          command: write-crate-version
          working_directory: ${{ matrix.path }}
          version: ${{ matrix.version }}

      - if: matrix.kind == 'npm'
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.path }}
        # Build matrix can target Windows runners; default shell there is
        # pwsh, but `if [ -f ... ]` is bash. Force bash for portability.
        #
        # Strict installs (`npm ci`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`) self-
        # heal to their non-strict form on failure. Why: bundled-cli / napi
        # consumers declare `optionalDependencies` for `<name>-<triple>@<version>`
        # platform packages that this pipeline produces. On the first publish,
        # those entries 404 on the registry; pnpm 10 silently drops 404'd
        # optionals from the lockfile when it is regenerated locally, then
        # `--frozen-lockfile` refuses on the next CI run because the lockfile
        # and package.json disagree. The `::warning::` makes the fallback
        # visible in the run log so the consumer understands the recovery.
        # See README → Recipes → Bundled-CLI npm family.
        shell: bash
        env:
          # #287: bundled-cli / napi consumers' build scripts read TARGET
          # to know which triple to cross-compile and stage under
          # `build/<triple>/<bin>`. Multi-mode (napi + bundled-cli)
          # consumers also read BUILD so a single script can dispatch
          # on the mode. Vanilla / `target == 'main'` rows ignore both.
          # Mirrors what `e2e-fixture-job.yml` passes to the same step
          # for the `js-bundled-cli` / `js-napi` fixtures; without this
          # block, the reusable workflow's contract diverged from the
          # fixture and consumers' first publish produced empty
          # `build/<triple>/` artifacts.
          TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
          BUILD: ${{ matrix.build }}
          # #627: the planned version. No engine-side writer runs on the
          # roll-your-own path, so a Rust build script must stamp its
          # Cargo.toml from $VERSION before cargo bakes CARGO_PKG_VERSION in.
          VERSION: ${{ matrix.version }}
        run: |
          if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then
            npm ci || {
              echo "::warning::package-lock.json drift (likely 404 on platform-package optionalDependencies for a brand-new bundled-cli/napi family); falling back to npm install"
              npm install
            }
          elif [ -f pnpm-lock.yaml ]; then
            # pnpm for the *consumer's* checkout, not ours. Deliberately a
            # literal and not ./packages/ci/actions/setup-pnpm: that action installs
            # our build toolchain, this installs theirs, and a `uses:` step
            # cannot appear inside a run: script anyway.
            npm install -g pnpm@11
            pnpm install --frozen-lockfile || {
              echo "::warning::pnpm-lock.yaml drift (likely 404 on platform-package optionalDependencies for a brand-new bundled-cli/napi family); falling back to pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile"
              pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile
            }
          else
            npm install
          fi
          npm run build --if-present

      # #384: stage the engine-built binary AFTER npm run build so it
      # always wins over anything a consumer build script stages to
      # `build/<triple>/` first.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'npm' && matrix.build == 'bundled-cli' && matrix.bundle_cli && matrix.target != 'main'
        name: bundle_cli — stage binary into ${{ matrix.artifact_path }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          CRATE_PATH: ${{ matrix.bundle_cli.crate_path }}
          DEST_DIR: ${{ matrix.artifact_path }}
          BIN: ${{ matrix.bundle_cli.bin }}
          RUST_TARGET: ${{ matrix.rust_target }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # #387: matrix.rust_target is the engine-resolved Rust triple
          # (plan.ts maps the npm-flavor matrix.target via toRustTriple).
          # #605: read from the declared triple's dir — zigbuild strips
          # the `.GLIBC_FLOOR` suffix from the output path.
          if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = "Windows" ]; then ext=".exe"; else ext=""; fi
          src="${CRATE_PATH}/target/${RUST_TARGET}/release/${BIN}${ext}"
          if [ ! -f "$src" ]; then
            echo "::error::cross-compile did not produce ${src}"
            ls -la "${CRATE_PATH}/target/${RUST_TARGET}/release/" || true
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p "$DEST_DIR"
          cp "$src" "$DEST_DIR/"
          echo "staged: $src -> $DEST_DIR/${BIN}${ext}"

      # ---- crates ----
      # cargo publish builds on the registry side; no artifact needed
      # at build time. The publish job invokes cargo directly.

      # #298: build-content guard. Permanent defense-in-depth — the
      # staged binary must exist at the path the engine's npm-platform
      # handler reads. Catches the bug shape this issue tracks (no
      # staging happened, the binary lives in the wrong directory)
      # and any future regression where the cross-compile silently
      # routes the binary elsewhere. Runs before upload-artifact, so
      # a broken per-platform tarball never leaves the build runner.
      # Mirror of the wheel-content guard added in #282 for pypi.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'npm' && matrix.build == 'bundled-cli' && matrix.bundle_cli && matrix.target != 'main'
        name: bundle_cli — verify ${{ matrix.artifact_path }}/${{ matrix.bundle_cli.bin }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          DEST_DIR: ${{ matrix.artifact_path }}
          BIN: ${{ matrix.bundle_cli.bin }}
          RUST_TARGET: ${{ matrix.rust_target }}
          GLIBC_FLOOR: "2.17"
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = "Windows" ]; then ext=".exe"; else ext=""; fi
          expected="${DEST_DIR}/${BIN}${ext}"
          if ! [ -f "$expected" ]; then
            echo "::error::bundle_cli staged binary missing at ${expected}"
            ls -la "${DEST_DIR}" || true
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "ok bundle_cli: ${expected} present"
          # #605: a Linux *gnu* binary must be DYNAMICALLY linked — a static
          # (static-pie) binary has no dynamic loader, so consumer dlopen
          # (SQLite extension loading) fails at runtime with `Dynamic
          # loading not supported` (dirsql#762). The portability property
          # the old #384 static assert guarded is enforced directly
          # instead: the binary's max versioned GLIBC_* requirement must
          # stay within the GLIBC_FLOOR the zigbuild linked against, else
          # it would fail at runtime on older distros (#381). Both are
          # gnu-lane contracts, hence the triple check — a consumer who
          # DECLARES a musl triple gets a static binary on purpose, and npm
          # ships it only where `libc: ["musl"]` matches.
          if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = "Linux" ]; then
            case "$RUST_TARGET" in
              *-linux-musl*)
                # A consumer that DECLARES a musl triple asked for a static
                # binary, and npm only ever installs that sub-package where the
                # synthesized `libc: ["musl"]` matches — a distro with no glibc
                # to dlopen against in the first place. The gnu-lane assertions
                # below would fail the row for being what it was configured to
                # be, and the ceiling check has no GLIBC_ symbols to read.
                echo "ok bundle_cli: ${expected} targets musl — static linkage is expected here; the dlopen / glibc-ceiling checks are gnu-lane only"
                ;;
              *)
                command -v file >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
                  echo "::error::required command 'file' not found on this runner — cannot assert linkage"
                  exit 1
                }
                if file "$expected" | grep -Eq 'statically linked|static-pie linked'; then
                  echo "::error::bundle_cli binary ${expected} is statically linked — a static binary cannot dlopen, so SQLite extension loading fails at runtime (#605, dirsql#762). Expected a dynamically-linked gnu build pinned to GLIBC_${GLIBC_FLOOR} via cargo-zigbuild."
                  file "$expected"
                  exit 1
                fi
                max_glibc=$(objdump -T "$expected" | grep -oE 'GLIBC_[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)+' | sort -uV | tail -1)
                ceiling="GLIBC_${GLIBC_FLOOR}"
                if [ -n "$max_glibc" ] && [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$max_glibc" "$ceiling" | sort -V | tail -1)" != "$ceiling" ]; then
                  echo "::error::bundle_cli binary ${expected} requires ${max_glibc}, exceeding the ${ceiling} portability floor — it would fail at runtime on distros older than the runner (#381, #605)."
                  exit 1
                fi
                echo "ok bundle_cli: ${expected} is dynamically linked, glibc ceiling ${max_glibc:-none} within ${ceiling}"
                ;;
            esac
          fi

      - if: matrix.kind != 'crates'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.artifact_name }}
          path: ${{ matrix.artifact_path }}

name: Actionlint

# Lints every workflow file under .github/workflows/. Catches:
#   - Bad action references
#   - Expression syntax errors
#   - Job/step dependency typos
#   - Shell script issues inside `run:` blocks (via shellcheck)
#
# Workflow YAML drift is expensive to debug -- the feedback loop is
# push → wait for runner → wait for step. Lint locally first.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '.github/workflows/**'
      - '.github/actionlint.yaml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '.github/workflows/**'
      - '.github/actionlint.yaml'

concurrency:
  group: actionlint-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  actionlint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # `dist-action/index.js` is gitignored on main and only exists on
      # tag commits (release-npm.yml folds it into the release commit).
      # actionlint validates `runs.main` paths exist for any local action
      # referenced via `uses: ./` — without the bundle present, the
      # e2e-fixture workflow's `uses: ./` step trips the existence check.
      # Build the bundle here so actionlint sees what runtime sees.
      - uses: ./packages/ci/actions/setup-node
      - uses: ./packages/ci/actions/setup-pnpm
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Build action bundle
        run: pnpm run build:action

      - name: Run actionlint
        run: |
          bash <(curl -sSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rhysd/actionlint/main/scripts/download-actionlint.bash)
          ./actionlint -color

      # Structural-safety invariant for the PR-time path
      # (issue #272 for build/_matrix; issue #317 for check). These
      # files must never grow `id-token: write` — that's what makes
      # it impossible for a PR-time invocation to inadvertently mint
      # an OIDC token capable of publishing. Any future patch that
      # adds OIDC there belongs in a new file on the publish path,
      # not these.
      #
      # The assertion logic lives in tested TypeScript
      # (`packages/ci/src/actionlint-idtoken/`, the
      # `piot-ci actionlint-idtoken` command), not inline bash — see
      # AGENTS.md > "Repo-internal CI gates" (#452, epic #442). The
      # `pnpm install` above links the `piot-ci` bin into
      # node_modules/.bin (its `prepare` builds dist at install time).
      - name: Assert PR-time path has no id-token permission
        run: pnpm exec piot-ci actionlint-idtoken

name: Advance v0 floating tag

# `v0` tracks main HEAD, not the latest release. Every push to main builds
# the action bundle, folds it into a tag-only commit (mirroring the Fold
# step in `release-npm.yml` — `dist-action/` is gitignored on main, so the
# tag must point at a synthesized bundle commit for `uses:
# thekevinscott/putitoutthere@v0` to resolve to a runnable action), and
# force-moves `v0` to that commit.
#
# Trailer-gated registry releases (`release: minor` / `patch` / etc.) still
# fire `release-npm.yml`, which cuts `putitoutthere-v0.x.y` tags. Those
# tags are the permanent per-release record. `v0` is the floating ref
# consumers compose against, and it stays fresh on every main commit.
#
# Concurrency: shares the `release` group with `release-npm.yml` so the two
# workflows serialize per repo. When both fire on the same push, the
# release workflow runs first (cutting versioned tags), then this workflow
# advances `v0` to a fresh bundle commit on top of main HEAD.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  advance:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: ./packages/ci/actions/setup-node

      - uses: ./packages/ci/actions/setup-pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build SDK
        run: pnpm run build

      - name: Build action bundle
        run: pnpm run build:action

      - name: Configure git
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

      # Mirrors `release-npm.yml`'s Fold step: stage the freshly-built
      # `dist-action/` bundle and create a commit on top of HEAD that
      # forwards the parent commit's full body (so any `release:` trailer
      # stays visible to the dogfood publish's plan re-derivation — see
      # `notes/handoff/2026-04-24-dist-action.md`). This is the exact same
      # `fold-bundle` engine command `release-npm.yml` invokes, differing
      # only in the commit subject.
      - name: Fold action bundle into v0 commit
        run: |
          pnpm exec putitoutthere fold-bundle --subject 'chore(v0): bundle action'

      # Force-move `v0` to the freshly-folded HEAD via the `advance-v0`
      # engine command, which shares `forceMoveTag` with
      # `advance-floating-major` so the two floating-tag movers can't
      # diverge (`src/advance-v0.ts`).
      - name: Force-move v0 to bundle commit
        run: pnpm exec putitoutthere advance-v0

name: putitoutthere build

# Reusable workflow for PR-time build verification.
#
# Consumer integration (their own .github/workflows/build-check.yml):
#
#   on:
#     pull_request: {}
#
#   jobs:
#     build-check:
#       uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere/.github/workflows/build.yml@v0
#
# Same plan + build matrix as `release.yml` runs, called via the same
# `_matrix.yml` reusable workflow. Stops there: there is no publish
# job, no `id-token: write` permission, no OIDC trusted-publisher
# exchange, no registry auth. The bytes required to publish do not
# exist on this code path. That structural guarantee — not a
# `dry_run: true` runtime flag — is what makes this safe to run on
# untrusted PRs.
#
# Permissions: contents: read only. A grep assertion in
# `actionlint.yml` rejects any future patch that adds `id-token: write`
# to this file or to `_matrix.yml`. See issue #272 for the
# safety reasoning.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      node_version:
        description: >-
          Node version for plan runners and for kind = "npm" build
          steps. Default `24`. Forwarded to `_matrix.yml`.
        type: string
        default: '24'
      python_version:
        description: >-
          Deprecated (#369): `kind = "pypi"` builds now fan across the
          Python versions inferred from each package's
          `requires-python` (or pinned via `python_versions` in
          `putitoutthere.toml`). This input no longer affects pypi
          builds; it is retained only so existing callers don't break.
        type: string
        default: '3.12'

# Ref-keyed group with cancel-in-progress: a new push on the same PR
# branch supersedes the in-flight build-check run. Releases (`release.yml`)
# use a repository-keyed group with cancel-in-progress: false, so PR
# build-checks and release runs never contend for the same slot.
concurrency:
  group: putitoutthere-build-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere/.github/workflows/_matrix.yml@v0
    with:
      node_version: ${{ inputs.node_version }}
      python_version: ${{ inputs.python_version }}

name: Changelog check

# Enforces AGENTS.md's "Changelog and migration policy": every PR that
# touches public-surface files must update both CHANGELOG.md and
# MIGRATIONS.md. Opt out per-PR by adding a commit with a
# `skip-changelog:` trailer (any value).
#
# The gate logic lives in tested TypeScript (`packages/ci/src/changelog-check/`,
# the `piot-ci changelog-check` command), not inline bash — see AGENTS.md
# > "Repo-internal CI gates" (#452, epic #442).

on:
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  check:
    name: Changelog check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: ./packages/ci/actions/setup-node

      - uses: ./packages/ci/actions/setup-pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        # packages/ci's `prepare` script builds its dist during install, so
        # `piot-ci` is linked into node_modules/.bin and resolvable below.
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Enforce changelog + migration entry
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: pnpm exec piot-ci changelog-check

name: putitoutthere check

# Reusable workflow for PR-time config validation.
#
# Consumer integration (their own .github/workflows/check.yml):
#
#   on:
#     pull_request: {}
#
#   jobs:
#     putitoutthere-check:
#       uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere/.github/workflows/check.yml@v0
#
# Green = "a release run from this commit would not surface
# configuration-level surprises." Runs every check that's knowable
# from the consumer's repo state alone (TOML parse, schema, common-
# mistakes detector, duplicate-name guard, depends_on cycle / dangling-
# ref detection). The complete pre-merge check list lives in #319;
# this file is the workflow shell (#317).
#
# Cheap: a couple of seconds per PR, no per-target build, no setup-
# python / setup-rust. The sibling `build.yml` runs the full plan +
# build matrix and is the heavier PR gate; `check.yml` is the
# config-sanity gate that catches `putitoutthere.toml` mistakes the
# build matrix wouldn't (since the build matrix only runs if the
# config parses far enough to produce a plan).
#
# Permissions: contents: read only. The PR-time surface must not be
# able to mint a publish token; emitting `id-token: write` here would
# turn this workflow into a parallel diagnostic surface that can act,
# which `notes/design-commitments.md` non-goal #8 forbids.

on:
  workflow_call: {}

# Ref-keyed concurrency: a new push on the same PR branch supersedes
# the in-flight check run. Mirrors `build.yml`. Releases (`release.yml`)
# use a repository-keyed group with cancel-in-progress: false, so PR
# checks and release runs never contend for the same slot.
concurrency:
  group: putitoutthere-check-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # Deliberately an explicit literal, NOT ./packages/ci/actions/setup-node.
      # This is a `workflow_call` workflow consumers invoke cross-repo
      # (`uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere/.github/workflows/check.yml@v0`),
      # so a `./` action path would resolve against *their* checkout, which
      # has no such action, and break every consumer. Same reasoning keeps
      # the literal in `_matrix.yml` and `release.yml`. See #591.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      - uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere@v0
        with:
          command: check

name: CI Gate

# Set this as the single required status check in branch protection, so
# adding a workflow doesn't mean updating branch protection.

on:
  pull_request:

concurrency:
  # A superseded gate run polls a stale SHA until it finishes. Cancel it.
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  monitor:
    name: CI Gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      # `resolve` below runs out of this checkout, so it must be installed first.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: ./packages/ci/actions/setup-node

      - uses: ./packages/ci/actions/setup-pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - uses: thekevinscott/pr-monitor@v1
        with:
          # `-C` because callbacks inherit the invoker's cwd, not the workspace.
          resolve-outputs: pnpm -C ${{ github.workspace }} exec putitoutthere resolve

name: Conventions
on: [pull_request]

# NOTE — we deliberately do NOT use the `e2e-verify` gate / e2e attestations.
# That gate is for repos that can't run e2e in CI; piot runs its full e2e
# suite in CI directly (e2e-cli.yml runs every tests/e2e/**/*.e2e.test.ts per
# PR; e2e-fixture.yml does the real-OIDC-publish runs), which is strictly
# stronger than an attestation receipt. `e2e-verify` is default-off until an
# `e2e-attestation` baseline is committed — we never commit one, so it stays

jobs:
  ci:
    uses: thekevinscott/testing-conventions/.github/workflows/testing-conventions.yml@v0
    with:
      source: packages/ci/src

  # runs with no `gates:` filter (epic #474 / #476). The only tuning is an
  # engine-scoped `config:` that sets the one_function_per_file ratchet and

  # It is kept separate from the ci job so its engine-only
  # `[[typescript.exempt]]` paths don't error against packages/ci/src; the ci
  # job keeps the default config and needs no exemptions.
  engine:
    uses: thekevinscott/testing-conventions/.github/workflows/testing-conventions.yml@v0
    with:
      source: packages/engine/src
      config: packages/engine/testing-conventions.toml
