        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          eval "$BUILD_COMMAND"
      - if: ${{ inputs.packaging_artifact == '' && needs.detect.outputs.packaging_build != '' }}
        name: Build the distribution (packaging_build)
        working-directory: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.package_root }}
        env:
          PACKAGING_BUILD: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.packaging_build }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          eval "$PACKAGING_BUILD"
      - name: Check the built distributions ship no test files
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
          PACKAGING_ARTIFACT: ${{ inputs.packaging_artifact }}
          PACKAGE_ROOT: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.package_root }}
          CLI_COMMAND: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.cli_command }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # nullglob: an unmatched glob expands to nothing, not the literal; globstar: `**` recurses.
          shopt -s nullglob globstar
          pkg="${PACKAGE_ROOT:-.}"
          if [ -n "$PACKAGING_ARTIFACT" ]; then dist_root=_packaging_artifact; crate_root=_packaging_artifact; else dist_root="$pkg/dist"; crate_root="$pkg/target/package"; fi
          checked=0
          check () {
            local lang="$1"; shift
            for dist in "$@"; do
              echo "::group::packaging --language $lang $dist"
              ${CLI_COMMAND:-npm --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP" exec --yes -- "testing-conventions${VERSION:+@$VERSION}"} packaging "$dist" --language "$lang"
              echo "::endgroup::"
              checked=$((checked + 1))
            done
          }
          check python "$dist_root"/**/*.whl "$dist_root"/**/*.tar.gz
          check typescript "$dist_root"/**/*.tgz
          check rust "$crate_root"/**/*.crate
          if [ "$checked" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::no recognized built distribution (.whl / .tar.gz / .tgz / .crate) found in '$dist_root' or '$crate_root'"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "checked $checked built distribution(s); no test files shipped"

name: E2E (CLI)

# Runs the node CLI e2e tier (tests/e2e/**/*.e2e.test.ts): vitest tests
# that shell out to the built CLI (a real `node` subprocess of the
# engine's bin) and hit the real registries, pointed at piot's own
# piot-fixture-zzz-* fixtures.
# Lighter than the fixture suite (e2e.yml): no publish happens, so it's
# reliable per-PR and its red->green is visible. See tests/e2e/README.md.

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: e2e-cli-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  e2e-cli:
    name: e2e (CLI, live registries)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: ./packages/ci/actions/setup-node

      - uses: ./packages/ci/actions/setup-pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: CLI e2e against live registries
        run: pnpm test:e2e

name: e2e fixture

# Reusable workflow that exercises a single fixture against the same
# job graph the consumer-facing reusable workflow runs
# (`.github/workflows/release.yml`). The contract is: for every distinct
# build-mode manifestation (one per fixture), the same plan → build →
# publish flow that consumers experience must succeed end-to-end against
# real registries via OIDC.
#
# Fidelity: every action call below (actions/setup-python@v6,
# PyO3/maturin-action@v1, actions/upload-artifact@v7, etc.) and the
# step ordering matches release.yml. The only difference is the
# "Materialize fixture" step that copies tests/fixtures/${{ inputs.fixture }}/
# into a fixture-tree/ subdir at workflow start, plus `uses: ./` (vs.
# `uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere@v0`) so the engine under PR review
# is the one being exercised.
#
# Internal — called only by .github/workflows/e2e.yml's matrix; not a
# consumer integration point.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      fixture:
        description: 'Fixture directory under tests/fixtures/ to exercise.'
        type: string
        required: true
      simulate_no_dist:
        description: >-
          #304 / #256 repro toggle. When true, the publish job clobbers
          `dist/` after build but before publish on first-publish rows,
          producing a tarball whose `files[]`-declared `dist/` directory
          is empty. The post-publish tarball-verify step is expected to
          fail on this — that's the demonstration that the assertion
          catches the cachetta 0.3.x failure mode. Off by default.
        type: boolean
        required: false
        default: false

concurrency:
  group: e2e-${{ github.ref }}-${{ inputs.fixture }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.matrix }}
      has_pypi: ${{ steps.has-pypi.outputs.has_pypi }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: ./packages/ci/actions/setup-node

      - uses: ./packages/ci/actions/setup-pnpm

      - name: Install engine dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build engine + action bundle
        run: |
          pnpm run build
          pnpm run build:action

      # Materialize the fixture as a fresh git repo at fixture-tree/.
      # `plan` mode wipes + copies the fixture, rewrites __VERSION__ to a
      # throwaway 0.0.{unix_seconds} (crates.io's immutable-publish rule
      # means each run needs a fresh slot), exports FIXTURE_VERSION,
      # uniquifies the `-placeholder` suffix on *-first-publish fixtures
      # (#304/#334/#294), and inits a throwaway git repo so the engine's
      # tag-creation path has a HEAD. Extracted to the piot-ci
      # fixture-materialize gate (#447) — the logic is unit-tested, not
      # inline bash. See packages/ci/src/fixture-materialize/.
      - name: Materialize fixture
        env:
          FIXTURE: ${{ inputs.fixture }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          RUN_ATTEMPT: ${{ github.run_attempt }}
        run: pnpm exec piot-ci fixture-materialize plan

      - id: plan
        uses: ./
        with:
          command: plan
          working_directory: fixture-tree

      # Mirrors release.yml: compute has_pypi for the caller-side
      # pypi-publish gate.
      - id: has-pypi
        env:
          MATRIX: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.matrix }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if printf '%s' "${MATRIX:-}" | grep -q '"kind":"pypi"'; then
            echo "has_pypi=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "has_pypi=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  build:
    needs: plan
    # Required: the default name interpolates run-scoped matrix fields
    # (`version`, and `name` on first-publish fixtures), so no predictor
    # can match it. These three are stable and unique per row.
    name: build (${{ matrix.kind }}, ${{ matrix.target }}, ${{ matrix.artifact_path }})
    if: fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix || '[]')[0] != null
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix) }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runs_on }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: ./packages/ci/actions/setup-node

      - uses: ./packages/ci/actions/setup-pnpm

      - name: Install engine dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build engine + action bundle
        run: |
          pnpm run build
          pnpm run build:action

      # #276: `build` mode materializes the fixture at a STALE baseline
      # (0.0.1), NOT matrix.version — mirroring a real consumer whose
      # pyproject.toml / Cargo.toml literal lags the planned version.
      # `_matrix.yml` bumps the manifest to matrix.version before maturin
      # runs; the post-build assertion verifies the artifacts agree with the
      # plan. build mode does no placeholder rewrite, no git init, and no
      # FIXTURE_VERSION export. Extracted to the piot-ci fixture-materialize
      # gate (#447); the gate is pure Node, so it behaves consistently across
      # the Linux/macOS/Windows build runners without the perl-vs-sed dance.
      - name: Materialize fixture
        shell: bash
        env:
          FIXTURE: ${{ inputs.fixture }}
        run: pnpm exec piot-ci fixture-materialize build

      # #391: mirror of `_matrix.yml`'s cargo cache step. The e2e mirror
      # is supposed to faithfully reproduce the engine path against the
      # fixture suite, so divergence surfaces here in PR CI rather than
      # in a downstream consumer's release pipeline. Without this step
      # the mirror would silently run cold while the engine runs warm —
      # both leaving #391's warm-cache acceptance unmeasurable on PR CI
      # and letting any future cache-dependent change pass here and
      # break in the wild. Gates, `shared-key`, and `workspaces` shape
      # match the engine step exactly; only the workspace paths gain a
      # `fixture-tree/` prefix because the e2e job materializes the
      # fixture under that directory just above (the "Materialize
      # fixture" step). See `_matrix.yml`'s twin step for the gate
      # rationale.
      - if: (matrix.kind == 'pypi' && matrix.build == 'maturin' && matrix.target != 'sdist') || (matrix.kind == 'npm' && matrix.build == 'napi') || (matrix.kind == 'npm' && matrix.build == 'bundled-cli' && matrix.target != 'main')
        name: cargo cache (#391)
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          shared-key: ${{ matrix.target }}
          workspaces: |
            fixture-tree/${{ matrix.path }}
            fixture-tree/${{ matrix.bundle_cli.crate_path }}

      # ---- pypi ----
      - if: matrix.kind == 'pypi'
        uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      # #276: bump the version source to matrix.version before maturin
      # reads it. Maturin reads [project].version from pyproject.toml
      # (or [package].version from Cargo.toml when pyproject declares
      # `dynamic = ["version"]`), with no env override. Without this
      # step, wheels ship at the literal on disk regardless of plan.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'pypi' && matrix.build == 'maturin'
        uses: ./
        with:
          command: write-version
          working_directory: fixture-tree/${{ matrix.path }}
          version: ${{ matrix.version }}

      # Mirrors release.yml: `maturin build --sdist` produces wheel +
      # sdist; use `command: sdist` for sdist-only.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'pypi' && matrix.build == 'maturin' && matrix.target == 'sdist'
        uses: PyO3/maturin-action@v1
        with:
          working-directory: fixture-tree/${{ matrix.path }}
          command: sdist
          args: --out dist

      # #610: `manylinux` mirrors the passthrough in _matrix.yml — empty
      # when the fixture sets no baseline (host build, unchanged),
      # otherwise the build runs inside the matching manylinux container
      # and the wheel gets the requested platform tag.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'pypi' && matrix.build == 'maturin' && matrix.target != 'sdist'
        uses: PyO3/maturin-action@v1
        with:
          working-directory: fixture-tree/${{ matrix.path }}
          command: build
          manylinux: ${{ matrix.manylinux }}
          args: --release --out dist --target ${{ matrix.target }}

      # #276: post-build assertion. The contract is "the build artifact
      # carries matrix.version" — verified directly against the produced
      # files, independent of which mechanism ensured the manifest was
      # correct, so it catches the divergence regardless of which build
      # path silently regressed. The find/extract/version-compare logic
      # lives in the engine now (`verify wheel`, #450, `src/verify/wheel/`)
      # as colocated-tested code with a pure-Node wheel-zip reader (no
      # `unzip`); this step is pure wiring.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'pypi' && matrix.build == 'maturin'
        name: Verify wheel/sdist version matches matrix.version
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          pnpm exec putitoutthere verify wheel \
            --path "fixture-tree/${{ matrix.path }}" \
            --version "${{ matrix.version }}" \
            --target "${{ matrix.target }}" \
            --manylinux "${{ matrix.manylinux }}"

      - if: matrix.kind == 'pypi' && matrix.build != 'maturin' && matrix.target == 'sdist'
        working-directory: fixture-tree/${{ matrix.path }}
        env:
          SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION: ${{ matrix.version }}
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip build
          python -m build --sdist --outdir dist

      # #324: hatch wheel-any row. Mirrors the matching step in
      # _matrix.yml (consumer-facing reusable workflow) so the e2e
      # fixture suite exercises the same build path real consumers do.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'pypi' && matrix.build == 'hatch' && matrix.target == 'any'
        working-directory: fixture-tree/${{ matrix.path }}
        env:
          SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION: ${{ matrix.version }}
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip build
          python -m build --wheel --outdir dist

      # ---- npm ----
      - if: matrix.kind == 'npm'
        uses: ./packages/ci/actions/setup-node
        with:
          registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'

      # #298: mirror of the _matrix.yml bundle_cli steps. The e2e fixture
      # job carries its own copy of the build steps (parallel to the
      # consumer-facing _matrix.yml). The cross-compile steps run before
      # `npm run build` so the crate is compiled with the right version
      # before the consumer's build script can execute.
      # #605: mirror of the _matrix.yml zigbuild lane; see that file's
      # bundle_cli `add Rust target` step for the rationale.
      # #384: the stage step runs AFTER `npm run build` so the engine-built
      # binary overwrites anything a consumer build script stages to
      # `build/<triple>/` under the same path.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'npm' && matrix.build == 'bundled-cli' && matrix.bundle_cli && matrix.target != 'main'
        name: bundle_cli — add Rust target
        shell: bash
        env:
          RUST_TARGET: ${{ matrix.rust_target }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # #387: matrix.rust_target is the engine-resolved Rust triple
          # (plan.ts maps the npm-flavor matrix.target via toRustTriple).
          # #605: register the DECLARED triple — no gnu→musl mapping. Linux
          # rows compile via cargo-zigbuild pinned to GLIBC_FLOOR, so the
          # binary stays dynamically linked (dlopen works, dirsql#762)
          # without inheriting the runner's glibc (#381).
          rustup target add "$RUST_TARGET"

      # Mirror of the _matrix.yml zigbuild step (#605): cargo-zigbuild links Linux binaries against a *chosen* glibc
      # (GLIBC_FLOOR) regardless of the runner's, replacing the #381
      # static-musl mapping — dynamic linking keeps dlopen working
      # (dirsql#762), the pinned floor keeps #381's portability. The
      # ziglang wheel supplies zig; cargo-zigbuild discovers it via
      # `python3 -m ziglang`. zig is a C cross-compiler too, so crates
      # with C source deps (libsqlite3-sys bundled, …) need no extra
      # toolchain.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'npm' && matrix.build == 'bundled-cli' && matrix.bundle_cli && matrix.target != 'main' && contains(matrix.target, 'linux')
        name: bundle_cli — install zigbuild toolchain
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          pip3 install cargo-zigbuild ziglang
          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      # #366: mirror of the _matrix.yml write-crate-version step. Bump
      # the crate's `[package].version` to matrix.version before
      # `cargo build` bakes CARGO_PKG_VERSION into the binary, so the
      # e2e fixture exercises the same pre-build version write a real
      # consumer's npm bundled-cli release does.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'npm' && matrix.build == 'bundled-cli' && matrix.bundle_cli && matrix.target != 'main'
        name: bundle_cli — write crate version for ${{ matrix.name }}
        uses: ./
        with:
          command: write-crate-version
          working_directory: fixture-tree/${{ matrix.bundle_cli.crate_path }}
          version: ${{ matrix.version }}

      - if: matrix.kind == 'npm' && matrix.build == 'bundled-cli' && matrix.bundle_cli && matrix.target != 'main'
        name: bundle_cli — cargo build for ${{ matrix.target }} (${{ matrix.bundle_cli.bin }})
        shell: bash
        working-directory: fixture-tree/${{ matrix.bundle_cli.crate_path }}
        env:
          RUST_TARGET: ${{ matrix.rust_target }}
          BIN: ${{ matrix.bundle_cli.bin }}
          GLIBC_FLOOR: "2.17"
          FEATURES: ${{ join(matrix.bundle_cli.features, ',') }}
          NO_DEFAULT_FEATURES: ${{ matrix.bundle_cli.no_default_features }}
        # See _matrix.yml's twin step for the bash-3.2-on-macOS rationale.
        # #337: pin --target-dir target so the binary lands at
        # <crate_path>/target/<triple>/release/<bin> regardless of workspace
        # structure. Mirrors the same fix in _matrix.yml.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # #387: matrix.rust_target is the engine-resolved Rust triple
          # (plan.ts maps the npm-flavor matrix.target via toRustTriple).
          # #605: Linux rows build via cargo-zigbuild with the glibc floor
          # pinned in the target suffix, so the binary is dynamically
          # linked (dlopen works — dirsql#762) yet floors at GLIBC_FLOOR
          # instead of the runner's glibc (#381). zigbuild strips the
          # suffix from the output dir, so artifacts land at
          # target/<triple>/release/ either way.
          case "$RUST_TARGET" in
            *-linux-gnu*)
              cmd=(cargo zigbuild --release --target "${RUST_TARGET}.${GLIBC_FLOOR}" --bin "$BIN" --target-dir target)
              ;;
            *-linux-musl*)
              # A consumer that DECLARES a musl triple gets zigbuild too, with
              # no floor to pin — musl has no glibc, and `<triple>.2.17` is not
              # a target zig accepts. It still needs zig: zig ships musl, so it
              # is the C cross-compiler these rows used to get from the apt
              # `CC_<triple>=musl-gcc` step this one replaced. Falling through
              # to a plain `cargo build` leaves them with no C toolchain at
              # all, and every crate with C sources — the ones a musl consumer
              # is told to vendor — fails to link.
              cmd=(cargo zigbuild --release --target "$RUST_TARGET" --bin "$BIN" --target-dir target)
              ;;
            *)
              cmd=(cargo build --release --target "$RUST_TARGET" --bin "$BIN" --target-dir target)
              ;;
          esac
          if [ -n "$FEATURES" ]; then cmd+=(--features "$FEATURES"); fi
          if [ "$NO_DEFAULT_FEATURES" = "true" ]; then cmd+=(--no-default-features); fi
          "${cmd[@]}"

      # #429: mirror of the _matrix.yml napi crate-version bump so the
      # js-napi fixture exercises the same pre-build path a real napi
      # consumer's release runs. Its Cargo.toml is colocated, so the write
      # runs; the polyglot-everything multi-mode fixture has no Cargo.toml at
      # packages/ts, so the guard skips it — same behavior as production.
      # `uses: ./` and fixture-tree-relative paths per the e2e harness.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'npm' && matrix.build == 'napi' && matrix.target != 'main'
        name: napi — detect colocated crate for ${{ matrix.name }}
        id: napi-crate
        shell: bash
        env:
          PKG_PATH: fixture-tree/${{ matrix.path }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -f "${PKG_PATH}/Cargo.toml" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::napi: no Cargo.toml at ${PKG_PATH}; skipping pre-build crate-version write (multi-mode / separate-crate napi)."
          fi
      - if: matrix.kind == 'npm' && matrix.build == 'napi' && matrix.target != 'main' && steps.napi-crate.outputs.present == 'true'
        name: napi — write crate version for ${{ matrix.name }}
        uses: ./
        with:
          command: write-crate-version
          working_directory: fixture-tree/${{ matrix.path }}
          version: ${{ matrix.version }}

      - if: matrix.kind == 'npm'
        working-directory: fixture-tree/${{ matrix.path }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          # napi / bundled-cli fixtures' build scripts read TARGET to know
          # which per-triple stub binary to stage. Vanilla / main rows
          # ignore it. Multi-mode fixtures (#dirsql) additionally read
          # BUILD so the same script can stage either family.
          TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
          BUILD: ${{ matrix.build }}
          # #627: mirror _matrix.yml so harness and workflow can't drift.
          VERSION: ${{ matrix.version }}
        # #305: mirror the #288 strict-install fallback from _matrix.yml
        # (the consumer-facing reusable workflow) into the e2e harness.
        # Without this, the e2e job's install step diverges from what
        # consumers actually run — and the js-bundled-cli-first-publish
        # variant (whose pnpm-lock.yaml is deliberately drifted to
        # reproduce #288) fails the build job at strict-install, even
        # though production's _matrix.yml would recover via fallback.
        run: |
          if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then
            npm ci || {
              echo "::warning::package-lock.json drift (likely 404 on platform-package optionalDependencies for a brand-new bundled-cli/napi family); falling back to npm install"
              npm install
            }
          elif [ -f pnpm-lock.yaml ]; then
            # pnpm for the *consumer's* checkout, not ours. Deliberately a
            # literal and not ./packages/ci/actions/setup-pnpm: that action installs
            # our build toolchain, this installs theirs, and a `uses:` step
            # cannot appear inside a run: script anyway.
            npm install -g pnpm@11
            pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-workspace || {
              echo "::warning::pnpm-lock.yaml drift (likely 404 on platform-package optionalDependencies for a brand-new bundled-cli/napi family); falling back to pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile"
              pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile --ignore-workspace
            }
          else
            npm install
          fi
          npm run build --if-present

      # #384: stage AFTER npm run build so the engine-built binary
      # overwrites any glibc binary the consumer build script staged.
      - if: matrix.kind == 'npm' && matrix.build == 'bundled-cli' && matrix.bundle_cli && matrix.target != 'main'
        name: bundle_cli — stage binary into ${{ matrix.artifact_path }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          CRATE_PATH: fixture-tree/${{ matrix.bundle_cli.crate_path }}
          DEST_DIR: fixture-tree/${{ matrix.artifact_path }}
          BIN: ${{ matrix.bundle_cli.bin }}
          RUST_TARGET: ${{ matrix.rust_target }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # #387: matrix.rust_target is the engine-resolved Rust triple
          # (plan.ts maps the npm-flavor matrix.target via toRustTriple).
          # #605: read from the declared triple's dir — zigbuild strips
          # the `.GLIBC_FLOOR` suffix from the output path.
          if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = "Windows" ]; then ext=".exe"; else ext=""; fi
          src="${CRATE_PATH}/target/${RUST_TARGET}/release/${BIN}${ext}"
          if [ ! -f "$src" ]; then
            echo "::error::cross-compile did not produce ${src}"
            ls -la "${CRATE_PATH}/target/${RUST_TARGET}/release/" || true
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p "$DEST_DIR"
          cp "$src" "$DEST_DIR/"
          echo "staged: $src -> $DEST_DIR/${BIN}${ext}"

      - if: matrix.kind == 'npm' && matrix.build == 'bundled-cli' && matrix.bundle_cli && matrix.target != 'main'
        name: bundle_cli — verify ${{ matrix.artifact_path }}/${{ matrix.bundle_cli.bin }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          DEST_DIR: fixture-tree/${{ matrix.artifact_path }}
          BIN: ${{ matrix.bundle_cli.bin }}
          RUST_TARGET: ${{ matrix.rust_target }}
          GLIBC_FLOOR: "2.17"
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = "Windows" ]; then ext=".exe"; else ext=""; fi
          expected="${DEST_DIR}/${BIN}${ext}"
          if ! [ -f "$expected" ]; then
            echo "::error::bundle_cli staged binary missing at ${expected}"
            ls -la "${DEST_DIR}" || true
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "ok bundle_cli: ${expected} present"
          # #605: a Linux *gnu* binary must be DYNAMICALLY linked — a static
          # (static-pie) binary has no dynamic loader, so consumer dlopen
          # (SQLite extension loading) fails at runtime with `Dynamic
          # loading not supported` (dirsql#762). The portability property
          # the old #384 static assert guarded is enforced directly
          # instead: the binary's max versioned GLIBC_* requirement must
          # stay within the GLIBC_FLOOR the zigbuild linked against, else
          # it would fail at runtime on older distros (#381). Both are
          # gnu-lane contracts, hence the triple check — a consumer who
          # DECLARES a musl triple gets a static binary on purpose, and npm
          # ships it only where `libc: ["musl"]` matches.
          if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = "Linux" ]; then
            case "$RUST_TARGET" in
              *-linux-musl*)
                # A consumer that DECLARES a musl triple asked for a static
                # binary, and npm only ever installs that sub-package where the
                # synthesized `libc: ["musl"]` matches — a distro with no glibc
                # to dlopen against in the first place. The gnu-lane assertions
                # below would fail the row for being what it was configured to
                # be, and the ceiling check has no GLIBC_ symbols to read.
                echo "ok bundle_cli: ${expected} targets musl — static linkage is expected here; the dlopen / glibc-ceiling checks are gnu-lane only"
                ;;
              *)
                command -v file >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
                  echo "::error::required command 'file' not found on this runner — cannot assert linkage"
                  exit 1
                }
                if file "$expected" | grep -Eq 'statically linked|static-pie linked'; then
                  echo "::error::bundle_cli binary ${expected} is statically linked — a static binary cannot dlopen, so SQLite extension loading fails at runtime (#605, dirsql#762). Expected a dynamically-linked gnu build pinned to GLIBC_${GLIBC_FLOOR} via cargo-zigbuild."
                  file "$expected"
                  exit 1
                fi
                max_glibc=$(objdump -T "$expected" | grep -oE 'GLIBC_[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)+' | sort -uV | tail -1)
                ceiling="GLIBC_${GLIBC_FLOOR}"
                if [ -n "$max_glibc" ] && [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$max_glibc" "$ceiling" | sort -V | tail -1)" != "$ceiling" ]; then
                  echo "::error::bundle_cli binary ${expected} requires ${max_glibc}, exceeding the ${ceiling} portability floor — it would fail at runtime on distros older than the runner (#381, #605)."
                  exit 1
                fi
                echo "ok bundle_cli: ${expected} is dynamically linked, glibc ceiling ${max_glibc:-none} within ${ceiling}"
                ;;
            esac
          fi

      # ---- crates ----
      # cargo publish builds on the registry side; no artifact needed
      # at build time. The publish job invokes cargo directly.

      - if: matrix.kind != 'crates'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.artifact_name }}
          path: fixture-tree/${{ matrix.artifact_path }}

  publish:
    needs: [plan, build]
    if: fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix || '[]')[0] != null
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: e2e
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
    # #304: Verdaccio service for first-publish e2e variants. Runs on
    # every publish job (always-on instead of conditional — GitHub Actions
    # doesn't support `if:` on `services:`, and the idle cost is ~3s of
    # container startup with no other side-effects). Steady-state fixtures
    # never resolve `localhost:4873` so the service has no influence on
    # their publish path. Per-job isolation gives us per-scenario wipe
    # implicitly: each fixture's publish job spawns its own service
    # container with empty volume state, so `npm view <name>@<version>`
    # is guaranteed 404 before publish without an explicit reset step.
    services:
      verdaccio:
        image: verdaccio/verdaccio:5
        ports:
          - 4873:4873
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: ./packages/ci/actions/setup-node
        with:
          registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'

      # npm Trusted Publishing landed in npm 11.5.1 (July 2025). Node 24's
      # bundled npm on the runner image may be older. Force the CLI up
      # so the OIDC-TP exchange path engages on `npm publish --provenance`
      # without a token (without this, the publish PUT goes out
      # unauthenticated and the registry returns 404 / 401-masked).
      # Pinned to an explicit major (not floating `latest`) so an upstream
      # release can only change CI's npm via a reviewed bump (#438/#439).
      # Was `npm@11` because npm 12.0.0's bundle omitted libnpmpublish's
      # unscoped `sigstore` dependency and every provenance publish died at
      # module load (npm/cli#9722); fixed in npm 12.0.1 (2026-07-10, npm/cli#9740
      # re-includes `node_modules/sigstore` in the packed tarball), so bumped
      # to 12.x per #440.
      - name: Pin npm to a Trusted-Publishing-capable version
        run: npm install -g npm@12

      # PyPI: upload step runs in the caller-side `pypi-publish` job
      # (mirrors release.yml). No twine / setup-python in the publish
      # job — the caller's job uploads, and since #623 cuts the tag too.
      # Fixture repos are throwaway git trees with no remote, so neither
      # half is observable here; the tag contract is pinned at the unit /
      # integration / CLI-e2e tiers instead.

      - uses: ./packages/ci/actions/setup-pnpm

      - name: Install engine dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build engine + action bundle
        run: |
          pnpm run build
          pnpm run build:action

      # `publish` mode recomputes the same throwaway version the plan job
      # baked in — the matrix's first-row version is canonical (every package
      # shares one version per run) — and is passed in as FIXTURE_VERSION via
      # `env:` (an `env:` value is templated safely; an inline `${{ }}` in a
      # run script is the #442 pre-shell-templating trap). It rewrites
      # __VERSION__, uniquifies the `-placeholder` suffix on *-first-publish
      # fixtures (#304/#334/#294), and inits the throwaway git repo — but does
      # NOT export FIXTURE_VERSION. Extracted to the piot-ci fixture-materialize
      # gate (#447). See packages/ci/src/fixture-materialize/.
      - name: Materialize fixture
        env:
          FIXTURE: ${{ inputs.fixture }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          RUN_ATTEMPT: ${{ github.run_attempt }}
          FIXTURE_VERSION: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix)[0].version }}
        run: pnpm exec piot-ci fixture-materialize publish

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          path: fixture-tree/artifacts

      - name: Authenticate with crates.io (OIDC)
        if: contains(needs.plan.outputs.matrix, '"kind":"crates"')
        id: crates-auth
        uses: rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action@v1.0.5

      - name: Export CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN
        if: steps.crates-auth.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          CRATES_IO_TOKEN: ${{ steps.crates-auth.outputs.token }}
        run: echo "CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN=$CRATES_IO_TOKEN" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      # #331: start an off-the-shelf cargo alt-registry that explicitly
      # accepts any token (and therefore needs no auth setup) as a
      # background process. Used both as the *primary* publish target
      # for any `*-first-publish` crates fixture (set
      # `PIOT_CRATES_REGISTRY_PRIMARY`, symmetric with how Verdaccio
      # backs npm first-publish) and as the *fallback* target on a
      # real-crates.io 429 (set `PIOT_CRATES_REGISTRY_FALLBACK`).
      # One registry serves both roles because the engine's seam
      # (`src/handlers/crates.ts`) distinguishes them via different env
      # vars.
      #
      # Tool: `cargo-http-registry` <https://github.com/d-e-s-o/cargo-http-registry>.
      # Per its README: "The created registry does not require any token
      # checks. As such, if being asked to cargo login to the registry,
      # any string may be used." That's the "Verdaccio for cargo"
      # property we need. A prior iteration on this issue wired Kellnr
      # (the production-grade self-hosted registry); three CI rounds
      # all 403'd because Kellnr deliberately rejects fixture-style
      # unrecognized identities. cargo-http-registry, alexandrie, ktra,
      # cratery, meuse were all surveyed; cargo-http-registry is the
      # only one that matches the no-auth-fixture shape and is
      # actively maintained (v0.1.8, Feb 2025).
      #
      # Cost: ~1-3 min `cargo install` cold (lightweight dep tree --
      # tokio rt-only + warp no-default-features + git2 + structopt,
      # no openssl-sys / sqlite-sys / aws-lc-sys). Acceptable in the
      # context of an e2e job that already runs 5-10 min; can be cached
      # in follow-up via Swatinem/rust-cache if the cost becomes
      # noticeable in practice.
      - name: Install cargo-http-registry (#331)
        if: contains(needs.plan.outputs.matrix, '"kind":"crates"')
        run: cargo install --locked cargo-http-registry@0.1.8

      # Backgrounds cargo-http-registry (detached) on the fixed port
      # 127.0.0.1:35503 — so the `PIOT_CRATES_REGISTRY_*` env values passed
      # to the engine step below are statically known — writing to a log
      # file and exporting its PID, polls the git-smart-http endpoint until
      # ready (the first call cargo makes), and on success appends
      # `[net] git-fetch-with-cli = true` to cargo config so libgit2 stops
      # choking on the alt-registry's `application/octet-stream` content-type
      # (the system git binary the flag routes to does not). On failure it
      # dumps the raw log and fails. Extracted to the piot-ci cargo-registry
      # gate (#454); see packages/ci/src/cargo-registry/.
      - name: Start cargo-http-registry (#331)
        if: contains(needs.plan.outputs.matrix, '"kind":"crates"')
        shell: bash
        run: pnpm exec piot-ci cargo-registry start

      # Mirrors release.yml: rebuild npm packages from source before
      # the engine's `npm publish` runs. The build job's dist/ is not
      # carried through as an artifact for vanilla npm rows.
      - name: Build npm packages
        if: contains(needs.plan.outputs.matrix, '"kind":"npm"')
        shell: bash
        env:
          MATRIX: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.matrix }}
        # #305: mirror the #288 strict-install fallback from release.yml
        # (the consumer-facing reusable workflow's publish job). Same
        # rationale as the build job's step above — the e2e harness has
        # to track the production install behavior or first-publish
        # bundled-cli/napi families fail in e2e while passing for
        # consumers.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          paths=$(printf '%s' "$MATRIX" | jq -r '.[] | select(.kind == "npm") | .path' | sort -u)
          for path in $paths; do
            echo "::group::npm install + build at fixture-tree/${path}"
            pushd "fixture-tree/${path}" > /dev/null
            if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then
              npm ci || {
                echo "::warning::package-lock.json drift (likely 404 on platform-package optionalDependencies for a brand-new bundled-cli/napi family); falling back to npm install"
                npm install
              }
            elif [ -f pnpm-lock.yaml ]; then
              # pnpm for the *consumer's* checkout, not ours. Deliberately a
              # literal and not ./packages/ci/actions/setup-pnpm: that action installs
              # our build toolchain, this installs theirs, and a `uses:` step
              # cannot appear inside a run: script anyway.
              npm install -g pnpm@11
              pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-workspace || {
                echo "::warning::pnpm-lock.yaml drift (likely 404 on platform-package optionalDependencies for a brand-new bundled-cli/napi family); falling back to pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile"
                pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile --ignore-workspace
              }
            else
              npm install
            fi
            npm run build --if-present
            popd > /dev/null
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done

      # TEMPORARY DIAGNOSTIC (#258): assert pre-publish state for each
      # npm main/noarch package. Fails the step (with the failure
      # annotation describing what's wrong) when:
      #   - package.json declares a directory in `files[]` that doesn't
      #     exist on disk (Build npm packages step didn't produce it), or
      #   - npm pack --dry-run wouldn't include that directory.
      # Strip once the verify failure root cause is understood.
      - name: Pre-publish fixture-tree assertion (diagnostic)
        if: contains(needs.plan.outputs.matrix, '"kind":"npm"')
        shell: bash
        env:
          MATRIX: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.matrix }}
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          rows=$(printf '%s' "$MATRIX" | jq -c '.[] | select(.kind == "npm" and (.target == "main" or .target == "noarch"))')
          fail=0
          while IFS= read -r row; do
            pkg_path=$(printf '%s' "$row" | jq -r '.path')
            pkg_name=$(printf '%s' "$row" | jq -r '.name')
            mapfile -t dirs < <(jq -r '.files[]? | select(contains(".") | not)' "fixture-tree/${pkg_path}/package.json")
            for d in "${dirs[@]}"; do
              local_path="fixture-tree/${pkg_path}/${d}"
              if [ ! -d "$local_path" ]; then
                listing=$(find "fixture-tree/${pkg_path}" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -printf '%f ' 2>/dev/null || true)
                echo "::error::[${pkg_name}] declared files[${d}] but ${local_path} does not exist after Build step. fixture-tree/${pkg_path} contents: ${listing}"
                fail=1
                continue
              fi
              count=$(find "$local_path" -type f 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
              if [ "$count" -eq 0 ]; then
                echo "::error::[${pkg_name}] ${local_path} exists but is empty"
                fail=1
                continue
              fi
              echo "OK pre-publish [${pkg_name}] ${local_path}: ${count} file(s)"
            done
            pushd "fixture-tree/${pkg_path}" > /dev/null
            pack=$(npm pack --dry-run 2>&1 || echo "(npm pack failed)")
            popd > /dev/null
            for d in "${dirs[@]}"; do
              if ! printf '%s' "$pack" | grep -q "${d}/"; then
                pack_compact=$(printf '%s' "$pack" | tr '\n' '|')
                echo "::error::[${pkg_name}] npm pack --dry-run does NOT include ${d}/. Full pack output: ${pack_compact}"
                fail=1
              fi
            done
          done <<< "$rows"
          exit "$fail"

      # #304 / #256: opt-in repro that clobbers dist/ between build and
      # publish on first-publish rows. The post-publish tarball-verify
      # step is expected to fail when this runs — that's the
      # demonstration that the assertion catches missing build output
      # against an empty registry. Skipped by default.
      - name: '#256 repro: clobber dist/ before publish (opt-in)'
        if: inputs.simulate_no_dist && endsWith(inputs.fixture, '-first-publish')
        shell: bash
        env:
          MATRIX: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.matrix }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          paths=$(printf '%s' "$MATRIX" | jq -r '.[] | select(.kind == "npm") | .path' | sort -u)
          for path in $paths; do
            target="fixture-tree/${path}/dist"
            if [ -d "$target" ]; then
              echo "::warning::#256 repro: clobbering ${target}"
              find "$target" -mindepth 1 -delete
            fi
          done

      # #304: configure Verdaccio auth for first-publish rows. Waits for the
      # Verdaccio `/-/ping` endpoint to bind, creates an `e2e` user via the
      # user-create endpoint, captures + masks the returned auth token, and
      # writes it into a per-package `.npmrc` so the subsequent
      # `npm publish --registry=http://localhost:4873` honors it. The
      # handler's PIOT_NPM_REGISTRY seam reads from `ctx.env` (npm.ts /
      # npm-platform.ts); it is set on the publish action step below, gated
      # to first-publish rows. Extracted to the piot-ci verdaccio-auth gate
      # (#453); see packages/ci/src/verdaccio-auth/.
      - name: Configure Verdaccio auth (first-publish)
        if: endsWith(inputs.fixture, '-first-publish')
        shell: bash
        env:
          MATRIX: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.matrix }}
        run: pnpm exec piot-ci verdaccio-auth

      - uses: ./
        env:
          # The repository-visibility preflight check calls the GitHub
          # API; an authenticated call gets 5000 req/hr instead of the
          # unauthenticated 60, so a multi-fixture e2e run never
          # rate-limits across its many publish jobs.
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # #304: routes the engine's npm handler at Verdaccio for
          # first-publish rows. Empty for steady-state rows so the handler
          # falls through to its normal real-npm + OIDC-TP path.
          PIOT_NPM_REGISTRY: ${{ endsWith(inputs.fixture, '-first-publish') && 'http://localhost:4873' || '' }}
          # #334: routes the engine's crates handler exclusively at
          # cargo-http-registry for first-publish crates fixtures
          # (rust-vanilla-first-publish today). The PRIMARY seam
          # short-circuits the real-crates.io publish path entirely
          # (no fallback, no 429-retry) — the symmetric counterpart of
          # PIOT_NPM_REGISTRY for the cargo handler. Empty for
          # non-first-publish or non-crates fixtures so the steady-state
          # OIDC-TP path through real crates.io is preserved.
          PIOT_CRATES_REGISTRY_PRIMARY: ${{ endsWith(inputs.fixture, '-first-publish') && contains(needs.plan.outputs.matrix, '"kind":"crates"') && 'http://127.0.0.1:35503/git' || '' }}
          # #331: routes the engine's crates handler at the alt-registry
          # ONLY on a 429 from real crates.io ("published too many
          # versions of this crate in the last 24 hours"). Steady-state
          # happy path still hits real crates.io via the OIDC-TP
          # exchange exported above; the fallback is opt-in (handler
          # only retries when this env var is non-empty) and emits a
          # `::warning::` in the log so a reviewer sees the path was
          # taken. Empty for non-crates fixtures so unset stays unset.
          # When PRIMARY is set above (first-publish crates fixtures),
          # the handler's PRIMARY branch is authoritative and ignores
          # FALLBACK on 429 — see src/handlers/crates.ts.
          PIOT_CRATES_REGISTRY_FALLBACK: ${{ contains(needs.plan.outputs.matrix, '"kind":"crates"') && 'http://127.0.0.1:35503/git' || '' }}
        with:
          command: publish
          working_directory: fixture-tree

      # #334: post-publish .crate tarball-verify gate for first-publish
      # crates fixtures. Symmetric with the npm "Verify published npm
      # tarballs honor package.json files" step below — assert the
      # just-published artifact contains what the engine planned to ship,
      # so a publish that no-op'd silently (or produced an empty .crate)
      # can't go green. The find/extract/source-present logic lives in the
      # engine now (`verify crate`, #449, `src/verify/crate/`) as colocated-
      # tested code, not inline bash; this step is pure wiring. cargo-http-
      # registry stores .crate files on disk under the registry root, so
      # the command reads them straight off `--registry-root` — no fetch.
      - name: Verify published .crate tarballs honor expected files
        if: endsWith(inputs.fixture, '-first-publish') && contains(needs.plan.outputs.matrix, '"kind":"crates"')
        shell: bash
        env:
          MATRIX: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.matrix }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          pnpm exec putitoutthere verify crate \
            --matrix "$MATRIX" \
            --registry-root "${RUNNER_TEMP}/piot-alt-registry"

      # #331: diagnostic dump for the cargo-http-registry alt-registry.
      # Runs on every crates-bearing job regardless of publish outcome
      # so the root cause is visible in the log if the engine's
      # fallback ever fires AND fails. Cheap on the happy path. Strip
      # once the alt-registry path has been stable in CI for ~10
      # polyglot runs.
      # Prints the grouped cargo-http-registry diagnostic dump: the raw log,
      # an endpoint HTTP-code probe, and the raw cargo config (with
      # (no log) / (no config.toml) fallbacks). Never fails (diagnostic
      # only). Extracted to the piot-ci cargo-registry gate (#454); see
      # packages/ci/src/cargo-registry/.
      - name: Diagnostic dump (cargo-http-registry)
        if: always() && contains(needs.plan.outputs.matrix, '"kind":"crates"')
        shell: bash
        run: pnpm exec piot-ci cargo-registry diagnose

      # Post-publish npm tarball verification lives in the engine now
      # (`verify npm-tarball`, #443): the `files[]`-dir presence check, its
      # packument-lag retry, and the local-state diagnostic are one
      # colocated-tested command instead of inline bash. Catches the
      # cachetta 0.3.x failure mode — build produces dist/, publish ships a
      # fresh tree without it, and `npm publish` returns 0 anyway.
      - name: Verify published npm tarballs honor package.json files
        if: contains(needs.plan.outputs.matrix, '"kind":"npm"')
        shell: bash
        env:
          MATRIX: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.matrix }}
          # #304: read from the same registry the engine just published to.
          # Empty for steady-state rows → real npm with the generous
          # CDN-propagation backoff; set for first-publish rows → Verdaccio
          # with the tight, immediately-consistent schedule.
          REGISTRY_URL: ${{ endsWith(inputs.fixture, '-first-publish') && 'http://localhost:4873' || '' }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--matrix "$MATRIX" --cwd fixture-tree)
          if [ -n "${REGISTRY_URL:-}" ]; then args+=(--registry "$REGISTRY_URL"); fi
          pnpm exec putitoutthere verify npm-tarball "${args[@]}"

      # #306: per-triple tarball-verify for first-publish napi / bundled-cli
      # fixtures. Symmetric with the main verify above and in the same engine
      # command (#443): asserts each synthesized platform package shipped its
      # binary (`.node` / executable), not a metadata-only tarball.
      - name: Verify published per-triple npm tarballs honor expected files
        if: endsWith(inputs.fixture, '-first-publish') && contains(needs.plan.outputs.matrix, '"kind":"npm"')
        shell: bash
        env:
          MATRIX: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.matrix }}
          REGISTRY_URL: http://localhost:4873
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          pnpm exec putitoutthere verify npm-tarball --per-triple \
            --matrix "$MATRIX" \
            --cwd fixture-tree \
            --registry "$REGISTRY_URL"

  # NOTE: the caller-side `pypi-publish` job lives in `.github/workflows/e2e.yml`,
  # not here. `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` aborts when invoked from inside
  # any reusable workflow (PyPA blanket-disables it; see
  # https://github.com/pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish/issues/166). The e2e
  # therefore mirrors the consumer pattern: the upload step runs at the
  # top level of `e2e.yml`, not here in the reusable. See
  # `notes/audits/2026-04-28-pypi-tp-reusable-workflow-constraint.md`.

name: E2E

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      simulate_no_dist:
        description: >-
          #304 / #256 repro toggle. When true, first-publish fixtures clobber
          their `dist/` directory after build but before publish, so the
          post-publish tarball-verify step fails. Use to demonstrate that
          the verify step actually catches missing build output against
          the empty Verdaccio. Off by default.
        type: boolean
        required: false
        default: false

concurrency:
  group: e2e-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  e2e:
    name: e2e (${{ matrix.fixture }})
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        fixture:
          - js-vanilla
          - js-vanilla-first-publish
          - js-napi
          - js-napi-first-publish
          - js-bundled-cli
          - js-bundled-cli-first-publish
          - js-python-no-rust
          - js-python-no-rust-first-publish
          - python-pure-hatch
          - python-pure-sdist-only
          - python-rust-maturin
          - python-rust-maturin-workspace-first-publish
          - polyglot-everything
          - polyglot-everything-first-publish
          - rust-vanilla-first-publish
    uses: ./.github/workflows/e2e-fixture-job.yml
    secrets: inherit
    with:
      fixture: ${{ matrix.fixture }}
      simulate_no_dist: ${{ inputs.simulate_no_dist || false }}

  # pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish aborts inside reusable workflows
  # (warehouse#11096), so PyPI upload has to live at the caller level.
  # See notes/audits/2026-04-28-pypi-tp-reusable-workflow-constraint.md.
  pypi-publish:
    needs: e2e
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: e2e
    permissions:
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: '*-sdist'
          path: dist/
          merge-multiple: true
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: '*-wheel-*'
          path: dist/
          merge-multiple: true
      # #294: discard first-publish wheels/sdists. They carry a literal
      # `_placeholder` token in the project-name half of the filename
      # (maturin normalizes the fixture's `-placeholder` suffix to
      # `_placeholder` in wheel/sdist filenames; the build job's
      # materialize step does NOT apply the `-placeholder` rewrite, by
      # design — see e2e-fixture-job.yml's plan/publish materialize
      # comments). Real PyPI has no Trusted Publisher record for these
      # uniquified names, so the pypa-publish PUT would 4xx. The
      # diagnostic surface that the maturin path provides on a
      # first-publish fixture is the in-job wheel-content guard
      # (e2e-fixture-job.yml lines ~233-274), not the upload to a
      # real registry — TP-shaped failure modes are explicitly out of
      # scope per issue 294.
      - name: Discard first-publish wheels (no TP record on real PyPI)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          dropped=0
          while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
            rm -f "$f"
            dropped=$((dropped + 1))
            echo "  dropped: $(basename "$f")"
          done < <(find dist/ -maxdepth 1 -type f \
            \( -name '*_placeholder*' -o -name '*-placeholder*' \) -print0 2>/dev/null)
          if [ "$dropped" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::warning::Dropped ${dropped} first-publish artifact(s) from dist/ — Trusted Publisher records are not provisioned for uniquified package names. The maturin build path on a first-publish fixture is guarded by the in-job wheel-content guard, not by the real-PyPI upload."
          fi
      - id: have-pypi
        run: |
          if [ -n "$(ls -A dist/ 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            echo "have_pypi=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "have_pypi=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
      - if: steps.have-pypi.outputs.have_pypi == 'true'
        uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
        with:
          skip-existing: true

  # #295: PyPI is the only registry with a public test instance whose
  # upload semantics match production closely enough to catch warehouse-
  # shaped failures before consumers hit them. Keep this as a separate
  # caller-side publish job for the same reason as `pypi-publish` above:
  # pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish aborts inside nested reusable workflows.
  testpypi-publish:
    name: TestPyPI publish + verify
    needs: e2e
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: e2e
    permissions:
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      # Toolchain for `pnpm exec piot-ci`. Checkout runs before the
      # artifact downloads so its workspace clean does not wipe dist/.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
